column1: # Safety classification of every first-party Rust file, for issue #121.
# The question each row answers is not "is this file important?" but
# "what breaks, and how quietly, if this file is wrong?"  Creusot is
# expensive, so it is pointed at the tier where a wrong answer is both
# severe AND silent -- tier S.  Everything else is named here with a
# reason, so the scope is a decision on the record rather than a gap.
#   S  determinism kernel -- a wrong answer silently breaks the
#      byte-for-byte reproducibility ADR-0004 promises.  Tests can miss
#      it because the run still completes and still looks plausible.
#   L  simulation logic -- gameplay truth.  A wrong answer is a bug, but
#      a loud one: the acceptance suites in tests/ observe it directly.
#   B  boundary -- C ABI and network wire.  Memory and protocol safety.
#      Covered by the Idris2 ABI model (#117) and the conformance
#      harness, not by Creusot; listed so the coverage claim is honest.
#   D  data and definitions -- serde content, constants, id newtypes,
#      registries.  Largely declarative; validated by round-trip tests.
#   P  presentation -- TUI and Bevy.  Derives nothing; renders tiers
#      above it.  A wrong answer is visible on screen.
#   T  tests, examples and binaries -- these observe the system, they do
#      not define it.  Verifying a test would be circular.
# Vendored code is NOT in this file and is excluded by path, explicitly,
# in scripts/creusot_check.sh -- see the VENDOR_EXCLUDED list there.
# The gate requires this file to be a BIJECTION with the first-party
# .rs files on disk: every file appears exactly once, every row names a
# file that exists.  A new .rs file therefore cannot enter the tree
